episode_title: Building in regulated industries in the age of AI

real_qa.q: How should health tech founders navigate reimbursement and payer incentives when building products in regulated healthcare?
real_qa.r: Successful players figure out a lane where they are not necessarily fighting the system but aligning with the interests of the party who is carrying the cost. The real big boss is reimbursement, not FDA approval. Your product is dead in the water even if it clears FDA if you skip reimbursement and what payers care about—like whether you reduce their cost or improve their efficiency.
real_qa.requete: health tech reimbursement payer incentives FDA

real_qa.q: What is the Advisory 5 methodology for turning reflection into action for founders?
real_qa.r: In Advisory 5 methodology, an action is not writing a business plan—it is doing something that gets the possibility of getting a no. Examples include asking a pilot customer to become permanent, making an ask of an investor, or doing something outside your comfort zone. The challenge is creating a space where action is the outcome of reflection, not just staying in the comfortable space of learning.

real_qa.q: How does Garner Health align incentives with employers in the healthcare benefits space?
real_qa.r: Garner Health works directly with employers who offer benefits to employees. They track metrics across thousands of physicians and millions of claims to see where those metrics produce the best outcomes. They help cover out-of-pocket expenses for going to the top provider, resulting in at least 12% savings for the employer without changing or touching the existing plan.

real_qa.q: What role does industry expertise play in de-risking early-stage healthcare startup development?
real_qa.r: Founders coming from outside healthcare often lack clarity on basic questions like whether they need FDA approval, which FDA path to take, or when to raise funding. Advisory 5 helps solve these foundational challenges by connecting early-stage founders with industry advisors in a curated, low-risk way through structured advisory boards, allowing founders to test advisor relationships before making permanent equity commitments.
real_qa.requete: healthcare startup FDA approval early stage founders

real_qa.q: How does Pump for Joy address the problem of working mothers in the health tech space?
real_qa.r: Pump for Joy founder saw a problem with working mothers who lack time to replace cleaning and maintaining feeding equipment for babies. She is building a kid cup that is disposable and biodegradable. After winning competitions and joining the Traction 5 program, she was able to raise almost $100,000 through WeFounder and join a female-focused accelerator program.
real_qa.requete: Pump for Joy disposable biodegradable feeding
